{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "visit_duration_min",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "visit_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clear, well-separated categories (acute, chronic, preventive, emergency, etc.) that can be grouped and compared against visit duration and urgency; interpretable and informative."
    },
    {
      "name": "primary_clinical_category",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Meaningful clinical domains (cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, etc.) enable segmentation; slightly fragmented but still interpretable and useful for exploring duration differences."
    },
    {
      "name": "symptom_acuity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Ordered severity scale (asymptomatic through life_threatening) is highly interpretable and directly relatable to urgency and duration."
    },
    {
      "name": "condition_complexity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Well-separated categories describing condition state; supports interpretable comparison against duration."
    },
    {
      "name": "injury_mechanism",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable mechanism categories that can be segmented on, though it is nearly duplicated by injury_or_illness_mechanism."
    },
    {
      "name": "diagnostic_workup_intensity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Ordered intensity levels are interpretable and plausibly co-vary with duration; the large NULL fraction (~40%) weakens comparison but categories remain meaningful."
    },
    {
      "name": "treatment_intensity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Distinct escalating treatment categories that segment cleanly and relate strongly to visit duration."
    },
    {
      "name": "disposition_signal",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clear discharge/admission outcome categories; interpretable and associational with duration and urgency."
    },
    {
      "name": "patient_age_proxy",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "Essentially restates the existing age_group focus dimension; adds no new external relationship and is heavily dominated by 'adult' (near-constant)."
    },
    {
      "name": "injury_or_illness_mechanism",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "Near-duplicate of injury_mechanism with almost identical value distribution; redundant and adds no distinct relationship."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 8,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.7,
  "rationale": "The set is largely strong for EDA: most added columns are external, interpretable categorical variables with well-separated levels (visit_type, symptom_acuity, treatment_intensity, disposition_signal, condition_complexity, clinical_category) that can be grouped and compared against visit_duration_min alongside urgency, department, and age group. Weaknesses lower the score: patient_age_proxy merely restates the existing age_group dimension, and injury_or_illness_mechanism is a near-exact duplicate of injury_mechanism, adding redundancy rather than new relationships; diagnostic_workup_intensity is diluted by a large NULL share. Overall the columns realise the exploratory-relationship claim well but not fully due to redundancy and restatement."
}
